required_outcomes: Does not instruct a chargeable repair or a contractor at the landlord's cost on the assumption that the oven is out of warranty, since the landlord asked for a free warranty repair.

Asks the landlord for what identifies the warranty route: who supplied and fitted the oven, roughly when, and any receipt, invoice, order confirmation or card statement, and whether the warranty was registered.
Asks the tenant for the oven's make, model and serial number (rating plate or a photo of it) and whether a manual or warranty card was left in the flat, so the manufacturer can be identified.
Tells the tenant the repair is being looked into under the warranty and what happens next, and holds the case or schedules a follow-up with a review date.
acceptable_alternatives: Checking the agency's own records for last year's oven replacement before asking the landlord, provided the landlord is still asked if nothing is found.
Offering the landlord a diagnosis-only visit while the warranty details are gathered, provided no chargeable repair is authorised without his agreement.
positive_behaviours: Notes that manufacturer warranties often run longer than 12 months, so an oven replaced last year may well still be covered.
Suggests the landlord search his email or bank statements for the order if the paper receipt is lost.
red_flags: Escalating to a human when gathering the installer and purchase details is routine.
Telling the landlord or tenant the oven is probably out of warranty without any evidence.
prohibited_actions: Instructing a contractor to repair the oven at the landlord's cost before the warranty route has been checked and the landlord has agreed to pay.
Inventing an installer, purchase date, model or warranty term.
critical_failures: Authorising a chargeable repair or approving spend at this point.
